title: Coordinated decommission & migration spec for legacy chatstream + model aliases
creator: Amaya Chen
description: PRD + migration playbook to retire the legacy /v1/chatstream endpoint and to remove historical model aliases. The goal is to require clients to use the unified /v2/chat endpoint and explicit model identifiers while preserving smooth migrations for production customers via canaries, dual-write compatibility mode, SDK adapters, and clear timelines. This document covers acceptance criteria, client guidance, communication artifacts, rollout and rollback plans, monitoring, and post-deprecation follow-ups.
background: We maintain a legacy streaming endpoint (/v1/chatstream) used by a subset of early PLG customers. Over time we introduced /v2/chat with a richer structured output, function/tool-calling, and a clearer model naming scheme. Concurrently, we created model aliases (e.g., redwood-chat-large -> rwd-chat-v2) to ease switching. Aliases and the chatstream endpoint complicate routing, observability, and kernel selection, and prevent us from enforcing versioned routing and improved SLA guarantees. This initiative consolidates traffic onto the unified API and explicit model ids and removes alias indirection to simplify runtime logic and reduce customer-serving surprises.
goals:
- Fully retire /v1/chatstream for public traffic and remove alias resolution backend logic by api-unify-2025.04 release.
- Ensure 99.9% of production traffic uses /v2/chat or explicit model IDs before alias removal.
- Provide SDK and server-side compatibility helpers so customers can migrate within a single release window.
- Maintain observability parity and no-regression on latency and token cost during and after migration.
non_goals:
- Rewriting customer prompts or performing application-level changes on behalf of customers.
- Replacing on-prem private deployment deprecation policies (those will be handled in a separate Private deployment plan).
scope:
In-scope: retire /v1/chatstream public route, add deprecation response headers for a 90-day overlap window, remove alias resolution service, SDK adapters for Node/Python/Go, console migration dashboard, migration docs and communication.
Out-of-scope: on-prem/appliance legacy endpoint removal (separate ticket), model architecture changes, and billing contract renegotiations.
requirements: 1) Server: Add reversible flag to enable/disable alias resolution and chatstream routing. 2) Server: Return X-Redwood-Deprecation, Retry-After, and X-Redwood-Client-Guide headers on /v1/chatstream responses during overlap window. 3) SDKs: Ship 0.1.1 adapters that transparently translate /v1/chatstream usage to /v2/chat and warn at runtime. 4) Console: Migration dashboard with per-customer usage and suggested migration plan. 5) Docs: Step-by-step migration guide, example curl and SDK snippets, and changelog entry. 6) Communication: Customer-ready emails, in-product banners for heavy users, and support playbook with escalation matrix.
acceptance_criteria:
- Automated integration tests verify that legacy streaming clients receive identical token sequences from the translation adapter for a representative set of prompts.
- Client SDKs published to package registries and validated by CI smoke tests.
- Console migration dashboard shows daily percentage of traffic still on /v1/chatstream and provides per-customer estimated work.
- Deprecation headers are present for all /v1/chatstream responses during the overlap period.
- No increase in 99th percentile latency beyond 10% across canary customers during migration.
- Product and Support run two dry-run migrations with at least one paying customer and record lessons learned.
- Alias resolution is feature-flagged off in staging and QA for 7 days without regressions prior to production removal.
migration_steps: 1) Prep: Create feature flag for alias-resolution and chatstream. 2) Instrument: Add metrics to track streaming vs unified endpoints, per-customer model id usage, and alias hits. 3) SDK release: Publish compatibility adapters and include runtime warning. 4) Overlap window (90 days): Keep /v1/chatstream functioning but return deprecation headers; enable dual-write routing for opt-in canaries (server duplicates requests to /v2/chat to validate outputs). 5) Canary: Select 5 low-latency customers, enable dual-write for 2 weeks, compare outputs; iterate on adapter. 6) Communication: Send staggered emails at 90/60/30/14/7 days before removal, publish migration guide, and update changelog. 7) Gradual throttling: After 60 days, apply soft throttles (rate-limit warning) for remaining heavy legacy traffic and provide priority migration assistance. 8) Removal: Disable alias-resolution flag and remove /v1/chatstream route in a controlled maintenance window with rollback capability. 9) Post-mortem: 2-week monitoring and incident retrospective.
client_guidance:
Summary: Clients should switch from /v1/chatstream to /v2/chat and pin explicit model ids (e.g., rwd-chat-v2-2025-01). We recommend: 1) Bump SDK to the provided adapter version. 2) If you rely on streaming chunk semantics, use the adapter which exposes an identical iterator API; test with a staging token. 3) Replace any usage of model alias strings in production; switch to explicit model ids to avoid surprises after alias removal. 4) Add the X-Redwood-Client-Version header to help us correlate migrations.
Examples: - curl: show example replacing /v1/chatstream with /v2/chat and adding model=explicit-id. - Node SDK: call client.chat.stream({model: 'rwd-chat-v2-2025-01', ...}) or enable adapterShim=true.
Failure modes: If clients cannot migrate before removal, support will offer a short-term paywalled migration route or a limited extension via support ticket.
communication_plan:
Channels: email (customer success), in-console banners, changelog, public docs, Slack #customer-success, and a dedicated migration support form.
Cadence: Announcement at T-90 days, reminder T-60 and T-30, migration webinars at T-45 and T-14, final warning at T-7, and sunset notice at T+0.
Templates: store email templates and in-product banner text in Confluence at the links section.
Support Playbook: triage guide, escalation contacts, sample migration commands, and priority support rules for enterprise customers.
timeline:
Phase 0 (2025-02-20 to 2025-03-05): Implement feature flags, metrics, and SDK adapter prototypes.
Phase 1 (2025-03-06 to 2025-03-20): Release SDK adapters, publish docs, open customer communications.
Phase 2 (2025-03-21 to 2025-05-19): 60-day overlap window with deprecation headers and canary dual-write.
Phase 3 (2025-05-20): Target removal of alias resolution and /v1/chatstream route.
Phase 4 (2025-05-20 to 2025-06-03): Post-removal monitoring and customer assistance.
rollout_plan:
- Stage: run flag off in staging for 7 days.
- Canary: enable dual-write for selected customers and verify parity with nightly diff jobs.
- Gradual: disable alias resolution for 5% of traffic, ramp to 25%, 50%, 100% across a 48-hour window while monitoring key metrics.
- Cutover: perform removal in a 30-minute maintenance window with on-call engineers present and automated rollback to re-enable alias resolution if error budget or key SLA is breached.
monitoring_and_metrics:
Dashboards: streaming-vs-unified, alias-hit-rate, per-customer legacy-traffic, 50/95/99 latency and token cost breakdown, error-rate by route.
Alerts: alias-resolution-error-rate > 1% for 10m, legacy-route-traffic > 5% after scheduled ramp, divergence-diff-rate from dual-write > 0.5% (investigate for model mismatch).
Validation: nightly diff report showing token-sequence alignment and semantic-check score across canary traffic.
rollback_plan: If parity divergence > 0.5% or 99th percentile latency increase > 10% during ramp, rollback steps: 1) Re-enable alias-resolution feature flag. 2) Re-open /v1/chatstream route. 3) Roll back SDK advisory and re-notify canary customers. 4) Run hotfix to fix mismatch and retry canary after sign-off.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Some customers depend on alias semantics (dynamic remapping) for A/B or fallback. Mitigation: Provide temporary alias bridge for enterprise customers with signed MSA and manual support.
Risk: Streaming semantics differ subtly. Mitigation: Provide an adapter with an experimental parity mode and run extensive dual-write comparisons.
Risk: Support load spike during deadline. Mitigation: Temporary increase in L2 support headcount + run migrations for high-value customers as part of program.
notes:
Action items: 1) ENG to add deprecation headers by 2025-02-25 (ENG-4321). 2) SDK leads to validate adapter API shape with DX by 2025-03-05. 3) CS to draft enterprise outreach list and prepare webinars.
Follow-ups: track per-customer migration blockers and create short-term extension policy for enterprise deals.
release_notes_draft: We are consolidating streaming and chat APIs to improve latency, observability, and model versioning. The legacy /v1/chatstream endpoint and model alias resolution will be retired on 2025-05-20. Please migrate to /v2/chat and pin explicit model ids. SDK adapters and migration guides are available — contact support if you need assistance.
